satuq-bughra-khan.s: Satuq Bughra Khan was a ruler of the Kara-Khanid Khanate in Central Asia and the first Turkic khan known to have converted to Islam, around 934. With Samanid support he took Kashgar, and his successors made Islam the religion of the state and its Turkic peoples.

sawlon.s: Sawlon was saopha of Mohnyin, a Shan state in northern Burma, in the early 16th century. He led a coalition of Shan states, including Mogaung, Bhamo and Momeik, against the Ava Kingdom, and in 1527 took Ava and killed its king.

sayajirao-gaekwad-iii.s: Sayajirao Gaekwad III was maharaja of Baroda from 1875 to 1939, chosen from a distant branch of the family after the British deposed Malhar Rao. He made Baroda one of the most progressive princely states, introducing compulsory primary education, a public library network, an…

sayf-al-din-suleyman-bey.s: Sayf al-Din Suleyman Bey was the founder of the Eshrefid beylik in central Anatolia, a descendant of the Turkmen commander Eshref. As Seljuk power waned in the 1280s he made Beysehir, on the lake of the same name, the centre of his principality.

sayyid-ali-kiya.s: Sayyid Ali Kiya was a Zaydi sayyid who founded the Kar-Kiya dynasty of eastern Gilan on the Caspian coast of Iran. Backed by the Mar'ashi rulers of Mazandaran, he took Lahijan and eastern Gilan around 1370.

scarpetta-ordelaffi.s: Scarpetta Ordelaffi was lord of Forlì in Romagna at the start of the 14th century and a leader of the region's Ghibellines. He welcomed exiled White Guelphs from Florence, including the poet Dante Alighieri, who stayed at his court around 1303.

scottish-highlands.s: The Scottish Highlands are the mountainous north and west of Scotland, beyond the Highland Boundary Fault. Home to Iron Age peoples recorded by Ptolemy and later to the Gaelic-speaking clans, they kept a distinct culture into modern times.

sea-of-marmara.s: The Sea of Marmara, the ancient Propontis, is an inland sea in north-western Turkey linking the Black Sea through the Bosporus to the Aegean through the Dardanelles. It separates Thrace in Europe from Anatolia in Asia.

sebastian-kindelan.s: Sebastián Kindelán was a Spanish army officer of Irish descent who served as governor of East Florida and later as captain general of Santo Domingo from 1818 to 1821. His rule fell in the period known as España Boba, when Spain neglected the impoverished colony.

second-anglo-maratha-war.s: The Second Anglo-Maratha War was fought between the British East India Company and the Maratha chiefs Scindia of Gwalior, Bhonsle of Nagpur and later Holkar of Indore. British armies under Arthur Wellesley and Gerard Lake won at Assaye, Laswari and Delhi in 1803.

second-balkan-war.s: The Second Balkan War was fought from June to August 1913 after Bulgaria, dissatisfied with the division of Ottoman lands won in the First Balkan War, attacked Serbia and Greece. Romania and the Ottoman Empire then joined against Bulgaria, which was quickly defeated.

secret-history-of-the-mongols.s: The Secret History of the Mongols is the oldest surviving work of Mongolian literature, written in the 13th century, probably soon after the death of Genghis Khan. It tells the story of his ancestors, his youth as Temüjin, his struggles with rival steppe peoples such as the…

seewoosagur-ramgoolam.s: Seewoosagur Ramgoolam was a Mauritian physician and politician who led the Labour Party and the island's independence movement. He was chief minister and then prime minister when Mauritius became independent on 12 March 1968, and held office until 1982.

seisyll-ap-clydog.s: Seisyll ap Clydog was an 8th-century king of Ceredigion in west Wales. He conquered the neighbouring kingdom of Ystrad Tywi, the Tywi valley, creating an enlarged realm named Seisyllwg after him.

semyon-mikhailovich-of-novosil.s: Semyon Mikhailovich was a Rurikid prince, a son of Mikhail of Chernigov, who was killed at the camp of Batu Khan in 1246. When his father's lands were divided, Semyon received Glukhov and Novosil on the upper Oka.

sena-gallica.s: Sena Gallica, modern Senigallia, is a town on the Adriatic coast of Italy, in the Marche. It was the main centre of the Gallic Senones, who settled the area after sacking Rome around 390 BCE.

sengge-namgyal.s: Sengge Namgyal was king of Ladakh in the western Himalayas from about 1616 to 1642, the greatest ruler of the Namgyal dynasty. He expanded his kingdom into western Tibet, conquering Guge, and built the royal palace at Leh.

sephardic-jews.s: Sephardic Jews are the Jewish communities descended from those of medieval Spain and Portugal, expelled in 1492 and 1497. Many settled in the Ottoman Empire, North Africa and the Netherlands, and from there in the Dutch and English Caribbean and Guianas.

seqenenre-tao.s: Seqenenre Tao was a king of the Theban Seventeenth Dynasty of Egypt in the 16th century BCE, when the Hyksos ruled the north from Avaris. He began open war against the Hyksos king Apepi.

serdar-berdimuhamedow.s: Serdar Berdimuhamedow is a Turkmen politician who became president of Turkmenistan in March 2022, succeeding his father Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedow after an early election. His succession established a family transfer of power in the authoritarian state.

serfoji-ii.s: Serfoji II was the Maratha raja of Thanjavur in southern India from 1798 to 1832. In 1799 he ceded the administration of his kingdom to the British, keeping the fort and an income.

sergio-mattarella.s: Sergio Mattarella is an Italian politician and jurist from Sicily who has been president of the Italian Republic since 2015, re-elected in 2022. A Christian Democrat, he entered politics after his brother Piersanti was murdered by the Mafia in 1980, served as a minister and…

serzh-sargsyan.s: Serzh Sargsyan is an Armenian politician from Nagorno-Karabakh who was president of Armenia from 2008 to 2018. His election was followed by deadly protests in Yerevan in March 2008.

setthathirath-ii.s: Setthathirath II, also known as Sai Ong Hue, was a prince of Lan Xang who grew up in exile in Vietnam. With Vietnamese backing he seized Vientiane around 1707 during a succession dispute, while Luang Prabang broke away under a rival line.

seuna-yadava-dynasty.s: The Seuna Yadava dynasty ruled much of the western Deccan in India from its capital Devagiri, modern Daulatabad, from the late 12th century. Former feudatories of the Western Chalukyas, they fought the Hoysalas, Kakatiyas, Paramaras and the Vaghelas of Gujarat.

sevappa-nayak.s: Sevappa Nayak was the founder of the Nayak dynasty of Thanjavur in Tamil Nadu. A noble of the Vijayanagara Empire who had married into the royal family, he was appointed to govern the Thanjavur region around 1532.

sfatul-tarii.s: The Sfatul Țării, the 'Council of the Country', was the regional assembly of Bessarabia formed after the Russian Revolution of 1917 and meeting in Chișinău. On 2 December 1917 it proclaimed the Moldavian Democratic Republic.

shah-beg-arghun.s: Shah Beg Arghun was the leader of the Arghun dynasty, Turko-Mongol nobles who had served the Timurids of Herat and held Kandahar. Driven out by Babur in the 1510s, he turned south into Sindh, defeated the Samma dynasty in 1520 and established Arghun rule in upper Sindh, with…

shah-mansur.s: Shah Mansur was a prince of the Muzaffarid dynasty that ruled Fars and central Iran in the 14th century, and its last effective ruler, seizing Shiraz in 1387. When Timur invaded again, he defied him and in 1393 led a desperate charge against Timur's army near Shiraz, where he…

shah-suwar.s: Shah Suwar was a ruler of the Dulkadirids, a Turkmen beylik on the frontier between Mamluk Syria and Ottoman Anatolia. With Ottoman encouragement he rebelled against the Mamluks in the late 1460s and defeated several Mamluk armies.

shahaji-bhonsle.s: Shahaji Bhonsle was a Maratha general in the Deccan and father of Shivaji, founder of the Maratha kingdom. He served the Ahmadnagar Sultanate and, after its fall to the Mughals, briefly propped up a puppet Nizam Shah until he surrendered in 1636.

shahr-yagil-yuhargib.s: Shahr Yagil Yuhargib was a king of Qataban, an ancient South Arabian kingdom with its capital at Timna in present-day Yemen. He is known from inscriptions in the Qatabanic language, which record building works and royal decrees.

shahrukh-bi.s: Shahrukh Bi was the leader of the Ming tribe of Uzbeks in the Ferghana valley and founder of the Khanate of Kokand. Around 1709 he broke away from the Khanate of Bukhara and established a separate state in the eastern Ferghana valley.

shakya-zangpo.s: Shakya Zangpo was the first ponchen, or civil administrator, of Tibet under the Sakya regime, appointed with the backing of the Mongol Yuan dynasty. While the Sakya lama Phagpa spent much time at the court of Kublai Khan, Shakya Zangpo governed from Sakya monastery, organised…

shams-al-din-ali-ibn-masud.s: Shams al-Din Ali ibn Mas'ud was the founder of the Mihrabanid dynasty of maliks in Sistan, on the borders of present-day Iran and Afghanistan. He established his rule in 1236, after the Mongol devastation ended the Nasrid maliks.

shams-al-din-muhammad-kart.s: Shams al-Din Muhammad Kart was the first malik of the Kart dynasty of Herat, of a family linked to the Ghurid Sultanate. The Mongols appointed him ruler of Herat around 1245, and the Great Khan Möngke confirmed him.

shamsuddin-ahmad-khan.s: Shamsuddin Ahmad Khan was nawab of Loharu and Firozpur Jhirka in northern India, son of the state's founder Ahmad Bakhsh Khan. In 1835 he was hanged in Delhi for arranging the murder of William Fraser, the British Resident.

shamsuddin-ilyas-shah.s: Shamsuddin Ilyas Shah was the founder of the Ilyas Shahi dynasty and of the independent Bengal Sultanate. Ruler of Lakhnauti, he conquered Satgaon and the Sonargaon Sultanate and in 1352 united Bengal as a single state, taking the title Shah-i-Bangalah.

shane-oneill.s: Shane O'Neill was an Irish chief of the O'Neills of Tyrone in Ulster. Rejecting his father's English earldom, he claimed the traditional title of The O'Neill and dominated Ulster in the 1560s, visiting Elizabeth I in London in 1562.

shang-yang.s: Shang Yang was a Chinese statesman and Legalist thinker, a nobleman of the State of Wey, who served Duke Xiao of Qin from 361 BCE. His reforms abolished hereditary privilege, rewarded farming and military merit, imposed harsh laws with collective responsibility and organised…

shankaraji-narayan.s: Shankaraji Narayan was a Deshastha Brahmin official of the Maratha state who was appointed Sachiv, one of the king's chief ministers, by Rajaram in 1697. He played an important part in the Maratha resistance to the Mughals in the hills around Pune.

sharif-kabungsuan.s: Sharif Kabungsuan was a Muslim preacher from Johor, of Arab descent, who arrived in Mindanao in the early 16th century. He spread Islam among the peoples of the Pulangi river basin and married into local ruling families.

shark-island-concentration-camp.s: The Shark Island concentration camp was a German prison camp on a small island off Lüderitz in German South West Africa, used during the war against the Herero and Nama. Prisoners, including Witbooi Nama deported after their rising, were held there in cold, harsh conditions…

shatt-al-arab.s: The Shatt al-Arab is the river formed by the joining of the Tigris and Euphrates in southern Iraq, flowing past Basra to the Persian Gulf. Its lower course, where the Karun joins it at Khorramshahr, forms part of the border between Iraq and Iran.

shavkat-mirziyoyev.s: Shavkat Mirziyoyev is an Uzbek politician who became president of Uzbekistan in 2016 after the death of Islam Karimov, whose prime minister he had been since 2003. He freed some political prisoners, ended forced labour in the cotton harvest, liberalised the currency and…

shaykh-uways.s: Shaykh Uways was sultan of the Jalayirid dynasty from 1356 to 1374, son of its founder Hasan Buzurg. He took Tabriz in 1360 and ruled both Iraq and Azerbaijan, the height of Jalayirid power.

shefqet-verlaci.s: Shefqet Vërlaci was an Albanian landowner from Elbasan and politician, a long-time rival of King Zog, who had broken off an engagement to his daughter. After the Italian invasion of 1939 he became prime minister of the Albanian Kingdom under Victor Emmanuel III, holding office…

sheikh-ali-khan-of-quba.s: Sheikh Ali Khan was the last khan of Quba, in present-day north-eastern Azerbaijan, son of Fatali Khan, who had united much of the region. After his father's death in 1789 the union fell apart.

sheikh-mujibur-rahman.s: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman was the leader of the Awami League and the founding leader of Bangladesh. After his party won the 1970 Pakistani election but was denied office, the army cracked down and he was arrested as independence was declared in 1971.

sheng-shicai.s: Sheng Shicai was a Chinese warlord who ruled Xinjiang from 1933 to 1944. Relying on Soviet military and economic support, he crushed the First East Turkestan Republic and other rebels, while running a harsh police state.

shi-chonggui.s: Shi Chonggui was the second and last emperor of the Later Jin dynasty in northern China, succeeding his uncle Shi Jingtang in 942. Unlike his uncle, who had been a vassal of the Khitan Liao dynasty, he refused to submit.

shi-siming.s: Shi Siming was a general of Sogdian and Turkic descent and a leader of the An Lushan Rebellion against the Tang dynasty. A childhood friend of An Lushan, he briefly submitted to the Tang after An's death, then rebelled again, killed An's son An Qingxu and proclaimed himself…

shibi-khagan.s: Shibi Khagan was ruler of the Eastern Turkic Khaganate from 609 to 619. He turned against the Sui dynasty and in 615 besieged Emperor Yang of Sui at Yanmen, in northern China.

shibl-al-dawla-nasr.s: Shibl al-Dawla Nasr was the Mirdasid emir of Aleppo from 1029 to 1038, son of the dynasty's founder Salih ibn Mirdas. In 1030 he defeated the Byzantine emperor Romanos III near Azaz, but then accepted Byzantine protection to secure his rule.

shimazu-nariakira.s: Shimazu Nariakira was daimyo of the Satsuma Domain from 1851 to 1858 and one of the most forward-looking lords of late Tokugawa Japan. He built Western-style reverberatory furnaces, shipyards, glassworks and factories at the Shuseikan in Kagoshima, and promoted able retainers…

shimazu-takahisa.s: Shimazu Takahisa was a Sengoku-period lord who reunited the rival branches of the Shimazu clan and the province of Satsuma by about 1550, ruling from Kagoshima. In his time Portuguese firearms reached Japan through Tanegashima in 1543, and he received the Jesuit Francis Xavier…

shivaji-ii.s: Shivaji II was a Maratha ruler, son of Rajaram and Tarabai, proclaimed chhatrapati as a child in 1700 with his mother as regent. When his cousin Shahu was released by the Mughals in 1707, a succession war followed, and Tarabai set up a rival court for Shivaji at Kolhapur.

shivaji-of-thanjavur.s: Shivaji was the last Maratha raja of Thanjavur in southern India, son of Serfoji II, ruling from 1832 to 1855 with the administration already in British hands. When he died in 1855 without a male heir, the British East India Company annexed Thanjavur under the doctrine of lapse.

shivappa-nayaka.s: Shivappa Nayaka was the greatest ruler of the Keladi Nayaka kingdom in coastal Karnataka, reigning from 1645 to 1660. He introduced a celebrated land revenue system known as the shist, based on a survey of the land.

sho-shisho.s: Sho Shisho was king of Chuzan on Okinawa from 1407 to 1421 and the founder of the First Sho dynasty. In 1406 he and his son Sho Hashi overthrew King Bunei and moved the capital to Shuri.

shobha-ram.s: Shobha Ram was an Indian politician from Alwar who led the government of the Matsya Union, the short-lived union of the princely states of Alwar, Bharatpur, Dholpur and Karauli formed in 1948. He served as its prime minister under the Rajpramukh, the maharaj rana of Dholpur.

sholoi-setsen-khan.s: Sholoi Setsen Khan was the first ruler of the Setsen Khanate, one of the khanates of the Khalkha Mongols in eastern Mongolia, in the first half of the 17th century. As the khanate lay nearest to Manchuria, he exchanged embassies and sent tribute to the rising Manchu state of…

shrinivasa-malla.s: Shrinivasa Malla was king of Lalitpur (Patan) in the Kathmandu Valley of Nepal in the second half of the 17th century. The son of Siddhi Narasimha Malla, he added buildings to the royal palace complex on Patan Durbar Square and restored temples.

shuja-al-din-khurshid.s: Shuja al-Din Khurshid was a Lur chief who founded the Khorshidi dynasty of atabegs in Lesser Luristan, in the Zagros mountains of western Iran. Around 1184, as the Seljuk Sultanate of Iraq declined, he took control of the region north of the Karkheh.

shukri-al-quwatli.s: Shukri al-Quwatli was a Syrian nationalist leader of the National Bloc who was elected president in 1943 under the French mandate. He led Syria to full independence when the last French troops left in April 1946.

si-inthrathit.s: Si Inthrathit, originally called Bang Klang Hao, was the founder of the Sukhothai Kingdom in present-day Thailand. With his ally Pho Khun Pha Mueang he drove the Khmer governor out of Sukhothai in the mid-13th century and became its king, founding the Phra Ruang dynasty.

si-renfa.s: Si Renfa was ruler of Mong Mao, a Shan state on the borders of present-day Yunnan and Myanmar, in the early 15th century. His expansion against neighbouring Chinese-recognised chieftaincies provoked the Ming dynasty, which launched the Luchuan-Pingmian campaigns from 1436 to…

si-satchanalai.s: Si Satchanalai is a historic city on the Yom River in northern Thailand, the twin city of Sukhothai and seat of its viceroys. It was a major centre of Sukhothai's ceramic industry, producing celadon wares in hundreds of kilns that were exported across Southeast Asia.

sibghatullah-mojaddedi.s: Sibghatullah Mojaddedi was an Afghan religious scholar from a leading Sufi family and leader of a moderate mujahideen party during the Soviet–Afghan War. Under the Peshawar Accord he became the first president of the Islamic State of Afghanistan in April 1992, serving for two…

sibylla-augusta-of-saxe-lauenburg.s: Sibylla Augusta of Saxe-Lauenburg was the wife of Margrave Louis William of Baden-Baden, the commander known as 'Turkish Louis'. After his death in 1707 she ruled the margraviate as regent for her sons until 1727.

sicilian-expedition.s: The Sicilian Expedition was the Athenian invasion of Sicily during the Peloponnesian War, launched in 415 BCE on the pretext of aiding Segesta against Selinus and aimed at Syracuse. It ended in 413 BCE with the destruction of the Athenian fleet and army at Syracuse.

sicilian-vespers.s: The Sicilian Vespers was the uprising that began in Palermo at Easter 1282 against the rule of Charles I of Anjou in Sicily. The island offered its crown to Peter III of Aragon, starting a long war between Angevins and Aragonese that split the old kingdom into a mainland part…

siddoji-rao-ghorpade.s: Siddoji Rao Ghorpade was a member of the Maratha Ghorpade family who took the valley of Sandur in the Deccan around 1713. His family had served Shivaji and his successors, and his descendants held Sandur as a small principality through the wars of the Marathas, Hyder Ali and…

sidney-hill.s: Sidney Hill is the Tadodaho, the chief who presides over the Grand Council of the Haudenosaunee, chosen from the Onondaga Nation. He has held the title since the early 2000s and has represented the Onondaga in their land rights claims, including the 2005 lawsuit seeking…

sidonio-pais.s: Sidónio Pais was a Portuguese army officer and politician who seized power in a coup in December 1917 and ruled the First Portuguese Republic as an authoritarian president. His regime, called the New Republic, was cut short when he was assassinated in Lisbon in December 1918,…

siemowit-ii-of-masovia.s: Siemowit II of Masovia was a Polish duke of the Piast dynasty, son of Bolesław II of Masovia. When his father died in 1313 the Masovian lands were divided among the brothers, and Siemowit received the southern part around Rawa, which he ruled until his death in 1345.

siemowit-iii-of-masovia.s: Siemowit III of Masovia was a Piast duke who reunited most of Masovia in the 1370s after the deaths of his relatives. A vassal of the Polish Crown, he issued a law code for the duchy and fostered its towns.

siemowit-iv-of-masovia.s: Siemowit IV of Masovia was a Piast duke of Masovia and a candidate for the Polish throne in 1382. He married Alexandra, sister of King Władysław II Jagiełło, and in 1388 received the land of Belz as a fief, beginning the Masovian line that held it until 1462.

sierra-leone-company.s: The Sierra Leone Company was a British chartered company founded in 1791 by abolitionists to run a settlement for freed Black people on the Sierra Leone peninsula. It took over the failed Province of Freedom, founded Freetown in 1792 with Black Loyalists from Nova Scotia, and…

siete-leyes.s: The Siete Leyes were seven constitutional laws adopted in Mexico in 1835–1836 that replaced the federal Constitution of 1824 with a centralist system. The states became departments under governors appointed from the capital.

sigismondo-pandolfo-malatesta.s: Sigismondo Pandolfo Malatesta was lord of Rimini from 1432 and one of the leading condottieri of Renaissance Italy. He commissioned the Tempio Malatestiano from Leon Battista Alberti and the Castel Sismondo.

sigmundur-brestisson.s: Sigmundur Brestisson was a Faroese chieftain and the central hero of the Færeyinga saga. Acting for the Norwegian king Olaf Tryggvason, he brought Christianity to the Faroe Islands around 999 and tried to bring them under Norwegian rule, opposed by the pagan chieftain Tróndur…

sigurd-syr.s: Sigurd Syr was a petty king of Ringerike in eastern Norway in the early eleventh century. He married Åsta Gudbrandsdatter, mother of Olaf Haraldsson (Saint Olaf), and with her was father of Harald Hardrada.

siyaj-kak.s: Siyaj K'ak' was a war leader linked to Teotihuacan whose arrival in the Maya lowlands in 378 CE marked the 'entrada'. Passing through El Perú-Waka', he reached Tikal on the day its king Chak Tok Ich'aak died, and installed a new dynasty there; inscriptions at Uaxactun and…

sikandar-begum.s: Sikandar Begum was the ruler of Bhopal State, first as regent and from 1860 as begum in her own right, the second of the four women who governed Bhopal between 1819 and 1926. She reformed its revenue and administration, stayed loyal to the British during the rising of 1857 and…

sima-yi.s: Sima Yi was a general and statesman of Cao Wei during the Three Kingdoms period. He defended Wei against Zhuge Liang's northern campaigns, destroyed the Gongsun regime in Liaodong in 238, and in 249 seized control of the court in a coup against Cao Shuang, laying the…

simeon-uros.s: Simeon Uroš was a half-brother of the Serbian emperor Stefan Dušan who governed Epirus and Thessaly after Dušan's death and claimed the imperial title in 1356. Ruling from Trikala, he relied on Albanian chiefs in Epirus, granting the title of despot to Peter Losha at Arta and…

simon-de-montfort-5th-earl-of-leicester.n: Simon de Montfort, 5th Earl of Leicester
simon-de-montfort-5th-earl-of-leicester.s: Simon de Montfort, 5th Earl of Leicester, was a French nobleman who led the Albigensian Crusade against the Cathars from 1209. He took Carcassonne and the Trencavel lands, won the Battle of Muret in 1213 and was invested with the county of Toulouse, but was killed by a stone…

simone-boccanegra.s: Simone Boccanegra was the first doge of the Republic of Genoa, elected for life in 1339 after a popular revolt against the noble families. He abdicated in 1344, returned as doge in 1356 and died, reputedly poisoned, in 1363.

simone-vignoso.s: Simone Vignoso was a Genoese admiral who captured the island of Chios from the Byzantine Empire in 1346 with a privately financed fleet. Because the Republic of Genoa could not repay the investors, the island was handed to them as a company, the Maona of Chios, which ruled it…

singhana-ii.s: Singhana II was the most powerful king of the Seuna (Yadava) dynasty of Devagiri in the western Deccan. He extended Seuna rule over most of Maharashtra and northern Karnataka at the expense of the Hoysalas and other rivals.

sitric-silkbeard.s: Sitric Silkbeard was a Norse-Gaelic king of Dublin from about 989 to 1036. He allied with Leinster against Brian Boru, and his side was defeated at the Battle of Clontarf in 1014, although Dublin itself was not taken.

sitting-bull.s: Sitting Bull was a Hunkpapa Lakota holy man and leader who united Lakota and Cheyenne bands against American expansion onto the Great Plains. His followers defeated Custer at the Little Bighorn in 1876.

sizzo-iii-of-schwarzburg.s: Sizzo III of Schwarzburg was a Thuringian nobleman who first called himself count of Schwarzburg in 1123, after the castle on the Schwarza river in the Thuringian Forest. He is regarded as the founder of the House of Schwarzburg, whose branches ruled principalities in…

skanderbeg.s: Skanderbeg, born Gjergj Kastrioti, was an Albanian lord who served the Ottomans and in 1443 broke with them and took Krujë. In 1444 he formed the League of Lezhë with other Albanian nobles and for twenty-five years resisted Ottoman campaigns, including sieges of Krujë.

slavko-kvaternik.s: Slavko Kvaternik was a Croatian army officer and Ustaše leader who proclaimed the Independent State of Croatia in Zagreb on 10 April 1941, as Axis forces invaded Yugoslavia. He served as its deputy leader and commander of the armed forces until 1942.

snorri-sturluson.s: Snorri Sturluson was an Icelandic chieftain, lawspeaker and author of the Prose Edda and the Heimskringla, a history of the kings of Norway. His sagas are a main source for the petty kingdoms of early Norway.

so-yoshitoshi.s: Sō Yoshitoshi was daimyo of Tsushima and head of the Sō clan, which managed Japan's relations with Korea. He acted as go-between before Toyotomi Hideyoshi's invasions of Korea in 1592, served in them, and afterwards negotiated the restoration of relations, concluded in the…

sobe-sonbai-iii.s: Sobe Sonbai III was the last ruler of Great Sonbai, the independent inland branch of the Sonbai kingdom in West Timor. He resisted Dutch control until a colonial campaign in 1906 captured him, and he died in exile.

socialist-revolutionary-party.s: The Socialist Revolutionary Party was a Russian agrarian socialist party founded in 1902 that drew on the populist tradition and the peasantry. It won the most votes in the 1917 Constituent Assembly election.

soest-feud.s: The Soest Feud was a war in which the town of Soest broke from its lord, the archbishop of Cologne, and placed itself under the duke of Cleves and count of Mark. The archbishop besieged Soest in 1447 with an army including Bohemian mercenaries but failed, and the town stayed…

soleyman-khan-ardalan.s: Soleyman Khan Ardalan was a wali of Ardalan, the Kurdish principality on the Safavid frontier with the Ottoman Empire. In the 1630s he founded Sanandaj (Sinneh) as the new capital of the Ardalan rulers, and the town remained the seat of the dynasty until its end in the…

solomon-ii-of-imereti.s: Solomon II of Imereti was the last king of Imereti in western Georgia, reigning from 1789 to 1810. He accepted a Russian protectorate in 1804 but resisted direct rule.

solomon-krym.s: Solomon Krym was a Crimean Karaite agronomist and liberal politician. After the German withdrawal in November 1918 he headed the second Crimean Regional Government, which relied on Allied warships and the White Volunteer Army.

somali-national-movement.s: The Somali National Movement was a rebel organisation founded in 1981, drawing mainly on the Isaaq clans of northern Somalia, to fight the regime of Siad Barre. The government's bombardment of Hargeisa in 1988 killed many civilians.

somba-opu.s: Somba Opu was the fortified royal capital and port of the Gowa Sultanate near modern Makassar in South Sulawesi. Its brick walls enclosed palaces and merchant quarters used by Malay, Portuguese, English and Danish traders.

someshvara-iv.s: Someshvara IV was the last ruler of the Western Chalukya Empire. In 1184 he recovered Kalyani from the declining Kalachuris and briefly restored Chalukya rule, but he was soon overwhelmed by the Seuna Yadavas and Hoysalas, who divided the former Chalukya lands of the Deccan…

soni-shah.s: Soni Shah was a Ponwar Rajput who had served the Bundela rulers of Bundelkhand. Around 1785 he seized Chhatarpur from the descendants of Maharaja Chhatrasal and founded his own state there.

sophia-albertina-of-sweden.s: Sophia Albertina of Sweden was a Swedish princess, daughter of King Adolf Frederick and sister of Gustav III. She became princess-abbess of Quedlinburg in 1787 and was its last abbess, as the imperial abbey was secularised in 1803 and passed to Prussia.

sophie-of-bar.s: Sophie of Bar was countess of Bar from 1033, a descendant of Duke Frederick of Upper Lorraine. Around 1038 she married Louis of Mousson, count of Montbéliard.

souda-bay.s: Souda Bay is a deep natural harbour on the north-west coast of Crete, near Chania. The ancient city of Aptera stood on the heights above it and controlled access to the bay.

soulbury-constitution.s: The Soulbury Constitution was the constitution of Ceylon drafted on the recommendations of the Soulbury Commission and brought into force in 1947–1948. It created a parliamentary system on the Westminster model and governed the Dominion of Ceylon after independence in 1948,…

sound-toll.s: The Sound Toll was a duty levied by the kings of Denmark on ships passing through the Øresund between the North Sea and the Baltic, introduced by Eric of Pomerania around 1429 and collected at Helsingør under the guns of Kronborg. It was a major source of royal revenue until…

sourigna-vongsa.s: Sourigna Vongsa was king of Lan Xang from 1637 to 1694, the kingdom's golden age, when Vientiane was visited by Dutch and Italian travellers. He died without a surviving adult heir, and the succession disputes that followed split Lan Xang into the kingdoms of Luang Phrabang,…

south-ossetia.s: South Ossetia is a region on the southern slopes of the central Caucasus, inhabited largely by Ossetians. Clashes there marked the Democratic Republic of Georgia in 1918–1920; it became an autonomous oblast in Soviet Georgia, broke away after the war of 1991–1992, and after…

south-tyrol.s: South Tyrol is the German-speaking Alpine region around Bolzano, south of the Brenner Pass. Napoleon attached it to his Kingdom of Italy in 1810, and it returned to Austria in 1815.

sovereign-principality-of-the-united-net.n: Sovereign Principality of the United Netherlands
sovereign-principality-of-the-united-net.s: The Sovereign Principality of the United Netherlands was the state formed in the northern Netherlands after French rule ended in 1813. William, son of the last stadtholder, returned as sovereign prince and accepted a constitution in 1814.

spanish-civil-war.s: The Spanish Civil War was fought between the Second Spanish Republic and the Nationalist rebels led by Francisco Franco, who rose in July 1936. Germany and Italy aided the Nationalists and the Soviet Union the Republic.

spanish-town.s: Spanish Town is a town in southern Jamaica founded by the Spanish around 1534 as Villa de la Vega, the capital of Spanish Jamaica. After the English conquest of 1655 it remained the island's capital and seat of its assembly until 1872, when the government moved to Kingston.

special-administrative-regions-of-china.s: The special administrative regions of China are Hong Kong and Macau, created under the principle of 'one country, two systems' when Britain returned Hong Kong in 1997 and Portugal returned Macau in 1999. Each has its own Basic Law, legal system, currency and customs territory,…

sremski-karlovci.s: Sremski Karlovci is a town on the Danube in Syrmia, now in Serbia. The Treaty of Karlowitz was signed there in 1699, and it became the seat of the Serbian Orthodox metropolitans in the Habsburg Monarchy.

sri-bata-shaja.s: Sri Bata Shaja was a ruler of the Rajahnate of Butuan in north-eastern Mindanao. Chinese records of the Song dynasty note that in 1011 he sent an embassy with tribute to the Song court, seeking equal diplomatic status with Champa, one of the earliest documented contacts…

sri-kesari-warmadewa.s: Sri Kesari Warmadewa was the first known king of the Warmadewa dynasty of Bali. He is named in the Belanjong pillar at Sanur, dated 914 CE, which records a military campaign and is the oldest dated inscription on the island.

sri-vikrama-rajasinha.s: Sri Vikrama Rajasinha was the last king of Kandy, reigning from 1798 to 1815, of the South Indian Nayak dynasty. His harsh rule alienated the Kandyan nobility, who conspired with the British.

srimara-srivallabha.s: Srimara Srivallabha was a king of the first Pandyan empire in southern India. He fought the Pallavas and the kings of Sri Lanka, and according to the Sri Lankan chronicle he invaded the island and sacked Anuradhapura.

saint-cadoc.s: Saint Cadoc was a sixth-century Welsh abbot, said to be the son of King Gwynllyw of Gwynllwg and a grandson of the royal house of Glywysing. He founded the monastery of Llancarfan in the Vale of Glamorgan, an important centre of learning, and his later Life preserves early…

st-georges-night-uprising.s: St. George's Night Uprising was a rebellion of the Estonian peasantry in Harju and other districts against their German and Danish lords, begun on the night of 23 April 1343.

stasioikos-ii.s: Stasioikos II was the last king of Marion in western Cyprus. In the wars of Alexander's successors he sided with Antigonus against Ptolemy I, who in about 312 BCE took the city, razed it and moved its people to Paphos, ending the kingdom.

statute-of-autonomy-of-catalonia-1932.n: Statute of Autonomy of Catalonia of 1932
statute-of-autonomy-of-catalonia-1932.s: The Statute of Autonomy of Catalonia of 1932 was the law of the Second Spanish Republic that gave Catalonia self-government under the restored Generalitat, with its own parliament and powers over education, culture, public order and civil law. It was suspended after the revolt…

statute-of-autonomy-of-the-basque-countr.n: Statute of Autonomy of the Basque Country of 1936
statute-of-autonomy-of-the-basque-countr.s: The Statute of Autonomy of the Basque Country of 1936 was approved by the Spanish Republican parliament in October 1936, after the outbreak of the Civil War. It created an autonomous Basque government, Euzkadi, under lehendakari José Antonio Aguirre, which in practice governed…

stefan-crnojevic.s: Stefan Crnojević was lord of Zeta from about 1451 to 1465 and the founder of the Crnojević state's power in the Montenegrin highlands. An ally of Venice and of Skanderbeg, whose sister Mara he married, he joined the League of Lezhë and held the mountain districts against the…

stefan-stambolov.s: Stefan Stambolov was a Bulgarian revolutionary and statesman. As regent after the abdication of Alexander of Battenberg in 1886, he secured the election of Ferdinand of Saxe-Coburg, and as prime minister from 1887 to 1894 he ruled firmly, resisting Russian influence and…

stefan-vojislav.s: Stefan Vojislav was the ruler of Duklja who threw off Byzantine authority in the 1030s. Around 1042 he defeated a large Byzantine army in the mountains near Bar, securing the independence of Duklja.

stefan-zeromski.s: Stefan Żeromski was a Polish novelist and playwright, author of Ashes and The Spring to Come. In the autumn of 1918, as Austrian rule collapsed, he headed the short-lived Republic of Zakopane, a local Polish authority in the Tatra mountains before the area joined the reborn…

stefanos-vogoridis.s: Stefanos Vogoridis was a Bulgarian-born Ottoman statesman of the Phanariot circle. In 1834 the Porte appointed him the first prince of the autonomous Principality of Samos, which he governed through deputies from Constantinople until 1850.

stepan-klochurak.s: Stepan Klochurak was a Ukrainian politician from Carpathian Ruthenia who led the local government of the Hutsul Republic at Yasinia in 1919, which sought union with the Ukrainian People's Republic. In 1938–1939 he was a minister of Carpatho-Ukraine, and he later spent years in…

stepan-razin.s: Stepan Razin was a Don Cossack leader who raided the Caspian coasts of Safavid Persia in 1668–1669 and in 1670 led a great rebellion of Cossacks and peasants along the Volga against the Russian tsardom. After defeat at Simbirsk, Don Cossack elders handed him over, and he was…

stepan-shaumian.s: Stepan Shaumian was an Armenian Bolshevik who led the Baku Commune, the Soviet government of Baku, in 1918. When the commune fell in July 1918 he and other leaders were arrested; they were shot by anti-Bolshevik forces in the Transcaspian desert in September 1918, remembered…

stephanus-schoeman.s: Stephanus Schoeman was a Voortrekker leader and commandant-general of the Zoutpansberg in the northern Transvaal. He resisted union with the other Boer republics, and in 1860–1862 he was a central figure in the civil war over the government of the South African Republic,…

stephen-i-of-hungary.s: Stephen I of Hungary was the last grand prince of the Hungarians and their first king, crowned in 1000 or 1001. He established the Catholic Church in Hungary, founded bishoprics and royal counties, and subdued rival chiefs such as the gyula of Transylvania.

stephen-i-of-iberia.s: Stephen I of Iberia was presiding prince of Iberia in eastern Georgia from about 590 to 627, of the Guaramid line. He built the Jvari church above Mtskheta, a model for later Georgian architecture.

stephen-ii-kotromanic.s: Stephen II Kotromanić was ban of Bosnia from 1322 to 1353. He enlarged the banate greatly, taking Hum (Zachlumia) around 1326 and lands towards the Adriatic, and sold Ston and Pelješac to Ragusa in 1333.

stephen-iii-duke-of-bavaria.s: Stephen III, Duke of Bavaria, was a Wittelsbach prince who received the duchy of Bavaria-Ingolstadt in the partition of 1392. His daughter Isabeau married Charles VI of France, giving the Ingolstadt line close ties with the French court.

stephen-tomasevic.s: Stephen Tomašević was the last king of Bosnia, reigning from 1461 to 1463, and briefly despot of Serbia in 1459. He refused tribute to the Ottomans and sought papal support, but in 1463 Mehmed II invaded, captured him at Ključ and had him executed, ending the Bosnian kingdom.

sthanu-ravi.s: Sthanu Ravi was a king of the Chera Perumals of Makotai in Kerala. The Tharisapalli copper plates of 849, issued in his reign, granted land and privileges to a Syrian Christian church at Kollam, and his court was allied with the Chola king Aditya I.

subhas-chandra-bose.s: Subhas Chandra Bose was an Indian nationalist leader, twice president of the Indian National Congress. Seeking foreign help against British rule, he went to Germany and then Japanese-held Asia, where in 1943 he proclaimed the Provisional Government of Free India (Azad Hind)…

sue-harukata.s: Sue Harukata was a senior retainer of the Ōuchi clan of western Japan who rebelled against his lord Ōuchi Yoshitaka in 1551, forcing him to suicide and installing a puppet. In 1555 Mōri Motonari defeated him at the Battle of Miyajima (Itsukushima), where he killed himself,…

suessa-aurunca.s: Suessa Aurunca was a town of the Aurunci in northern Campania, now Sessa Aurunca. After the Romans destroyed the Aurunci in the later fourth century BCE, a Latin colony was founded there in 313 BCE.

sujan-singh-of-shahpura.s: Sujan Singh of Shahpura was a Rajput of the Ranawat branch of the Sisodia house of Mewar. In 1629 the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan granted him the lands of Shahpura in Rajasthan, named after the emperor, and he founded the line of rulers who held Shahpura as a princely state…

sukarno.s: Sukarno was the leader of the Indonesian independence movement and the first president of Indonesia. He proclaimed independence on 17 August 1945, led the republic through the war with the Netherlands and the short-lived United States of Indonesia, and from 1959 ruled through…

sulayman-al-baruni.s: Sulayman al-Baruni was an Ibadi Berber scholar and politician from the Nafusa Mountains of Libya. A member of the Ottoman parliament, he led resistance to the Italian invasion from 1911 and in 1918 was one of the leaders of the Tripolitanian Republic.

sulayman-ibn-hud.s: Sulayman ibn Hud, known as al-Musta'in, was the founder of the Banu Hud dynasty of the Taifa of Zaragoza. He took power around 1039 after the murder of the last Tujibid ruler, and before his death in 1046 divided his lands among his sons, among them Ahmad al-Muqtadir, who…

sulayman-ibn-muhammad-al-hamid.s: Sulayman ibn Muhammad Al Hamid was emir of the Banu Khalid, who ruled al-Hasa in eastern Arabia, in the mid-eighteenth century. He pressured the town of Uyayna to expel the religious reformer Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab around 1744.

sulayman-ibn-sulayman-al-nabhani.s: Sulayman ibn Sulayman al-Nabhani was a ruler of the Nabhani dynasty of Oman, remembered as a poet-king. The Nabhani era, between the imamates, is poorly documented, but his Arabic poetry was collected in a diwan and is among the best known literary works of medieval Oman.

suleiman-ibn-qutalmish.s: Suleiman ibn Qutalmish was a Seljuk prince who founded the Sultanate of Rum in Anatolia. Taking advantage of Byzantine civil wars after Manzikert, he seized Nicaea around 1075 and Antioch in 1084, displacing local lords such as Philaretos Brachamios.

sulejman-vokshi.s: Sulejman Vokshi was an Albanian military leader from Gjakova and a commander of the League of Prizren, formed in 1878 to resist the transfer of Albanian-inhabited lands to Montenegro and Serbia. He led the League's forces until the Ottoman army suppressed it in 1881.

suleyman-askeri.s: Süleyman Askerî was an Ottoman officer of the Special Organisation. In 1913, during the Second Balkan War, he led the irregular forces that set up the Provisional Government of Western Thrace at Gümülcine against Bulgaria.

suleyman-ii-of-eshref.s: Suleyman II was the last bey of the Eshrefids, a Turkmen beylik centred on Beyşehir in central Anatolia. In 1326 he was executed by Timurtash, the Ilkhanid governor of Anatolia, who was reasserting Mongol authority over the beyliks, and his lands passed to the neighbouring…

suleyman-shah-of-germiyan.s: Suleyman Shah was a bey of Germiyan, a Turkish principality centred on Kütahya in western Anatolia. Around 1381 he married his daughter to the future Ottoman sultan Bayezid I, giving much of his land, including Kütahya, as her dowry.

sultan-ageng-tirtayasa.s: Sultan Ageng Tirtayasa was ruler of the Banten Sultanate in western Java from 1651 to 1683, under whom Banten became a great pepper port trading with Europeans and Asians alike. In 1677 he partitioned Cirebon among its princes.

sultan-al-atrash.s: Sultan al-Atrash was a Druze leader from Jabal al-Druze in southern Syria. He fought in the Arab Revolt against the Ottomans and in 1925 began the Great Syrian Revolt against the French Mandate, which spread to Damascus before it was crushed in 1927.

sultan-bin-saqr-al-qasimi.s: Sultan bin Saqr Al Qasimi was sheikh of the Qawasim of Ras al-Khaimah and Sharjah for most of the period from 1803 to 1866. After British attacks on Ras al-Khaimah in 1809 and 1819 he made Sharjah the family's chief seat, and he signed the General Maritime Treaty of 1820 and…

sultan-hadlirin.s: Sultan Hadlirin was ruler of Kalinyamat near Jepara on the north coast of Java and husband of a daughter of Sultan Trenggana of Demak. During the Demak succession war he was murdered in 1549 by agents of Arya Penangsang, and his widow, Ratu Kalinyamat, ruled after him.

sultan-husayn-wali.s: Sultan Husayn Wali was emir of Bahdinan, the Kurdish principality centred on Amadiya in northern Iraq, in the sixteenth century. He was a notable ally of the Ottoman Empire in its wars with the Safavids, and under him Bahdinan became a hereditary Ottoman vassal state known for…

sultan-said-khan.s: Sultan Said Khan was a Chagatai prince who founded the Yarkent Khanate in the Tarim Basin in 1514, taking Kashgar and Yarkand from the Dughlat lord Mirza Abu Bakr. A cousin and ally of Babur, he ruled until his death in 1533 during a campaign against Ladakh and Kashmir.

sultan-shah-ibn-ridwan.s: Sultan Shah ibn Ridwan was the last Seljuk ruler of Aleppo, a son of Ridwan. He succeeded his brother Alp Arslan al-Akhras in 1114 but was a puppet of the eunuch Lu'lu' and other officers.

sultan-tangkal-alam-bagagar.s: Sultan Tangkal Alam Bagagar was the last ruler of the Pagaruyung kingdom in the Minangkabau highlands of Sumatra. Acting as regent after the Padri War devastated the royal family, he accepted Dutch intervention, but in 1833 the Dutch arrested him for plotting against them and…

sultan-thaha-saifuddin.s: Sultan Thaha Saifuddin was ruler of the Jambi Sultanate in Sumatra from 1855. He refused to renew treaties with the Dutch, who deposed him in 1858, but he led resistance from the interior for more than forty years until he was killed in 1904, after which Jambi was annexed to…

sumyafa-ashwa.s: Sumyafa Ashwa was a Himyarite Christian installed by the Aksumite king Kaleb as ruler of Himyar in Yemen after the defeat of Yusuf Dhu Nuwas around 525. Within a few years the Aksumite soldier Abraha overthrew him and made himself king, ruling nominally under Aksum.

sun-ce.s: Sun Ce was a warlord of the late Eastern Han who conquered the lands south of the lower Yangtze in the 190s. He broke with Yuan Shu when Yuan declared himself emperor of Zhongjia in 197.

sun-en.s: Sun En was a leader of the Five Pecks of Rice Daoist sect who led a great rebellion along the south-east coast of Eastern Jin China from 399. His seaborne forces threatened the capital Jiankang before being repelled; he drowned himself in 402.

sunan-prapen.s: Sunan Prapen was the most influential ruler of Giri Kedaton, the religious principality near Gresik in eastern Java founded by Sunan Giri. In the later sixteenth century he sent preachers to Lombok, Sulawesi and the Moluccas and gave religious sanction to the rulers of Pajang…

sungai-ujong.s: Sungai Ujong was a Minangkabau chiefdom on the west coast of the Malay Peninsula, one of the states of the Negeri Sembilan confederacy, centred on modern Seremban. Rivalries over its tin mines brought British intervention in 1874, and it became part of the reconstituted Negeri…

supreme-commander-for-the-allied-powers.n: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
supreme-commander-for-the-allied-powers.s: The Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP) was the title of the head of the Allied occupation of Japan, held by General Douglas MacArthur from 1945 and by Matthew Ridgway from 1951, and the name of his headquarters in Tokyo. Working through the Japanese government,…

supreme-leader-of-iran.s: The Supreme Leader of Iran is the highest office of the Islamic Republic of Iran, created by the constitution of 1979 on the principle of the guardianship of the Islamic jurist. Held first by Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini and from 1989 by Ali Khamenei, it commands the armed…

suqut-al-barghawati.s: Suqut al-Barghawati was a former slave of Barghawata origin who served the Hammudid rulers and became master of Ceuta and Tangier in the mid-11th century. He ruled Ceuta as an independent taifa lord and resisted the advancing Almoravids, who defeated and killed him around 1079.

suraj-mal.s: Suraj Mal (1707–1763) was the Jat ruler of Bharatpur who turned his family's holdings west of Agra into a powerful kingdom. He built the fortress of Lohagarh at Bharatpur, took Agra in 1761 and profited from the weakness of the Mughals and the Maratha defeat at Panipat.

sutton-hoo.s: Sutton Hoo is a site near Woodbridge in Suffolk, England, with a cemetery of early 7th-century burial mounds. Its great ship burial, excavated in 1939, held a helmet, a gold buckle, shoulder clasps and silver from the Byzantine world, and is widely thought to be the grave of…

svetozar-marovic.s: Svetozar Marović (born 1955) is a Montenegrin politician who was the first and only President of Serbia and Montenegro, from 2003 to 2006. A senior figure of the Democratic Party of Socialists, he led the loose state union created in 2003 until Montenegro's independence…

svetozar-pribicevic.s: Svetozar Pribićević (1875–1936) was a Serb politician from Croatia who led the Croat-Serb Coalition in Austria-Hungary. In 1918 he was vice-president of the National Council of the State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs and pressed for its quick union with Serbia.

sviatoslav-ii-of-kiev.s: Sviatoslav II (1027–1076) was a son of Yaroslav the Wise who received Chernigov under his father's will in 1054. In 1073 he drove his brother Iziaslav from Kiev and ruled as grand prince until his death.

sviatoslav-vsevolodovich.s: Sviatoslav Vsevolodovich (1196–1252) was a son of Vsevolod the Big Nest of Vladimir-Suzdal and prince of Yuryev-Polsky. He built the richly carved white-stone Cathedral of St George there in the 1230s.

swathi-thirunal.s: Swathi Thirunal Rama Varma (1813–1846) was Maharaja of Travancore from 1829 to 1846. A patron of learning and the arts, he founded an observatory, a public library and an English school in Thiruvananthapuram, and composed hundreds of works of Carnatic music.

swedish-estonia.s: Swedish Estonia was the Duchy of Estonia under the Swedish crown from 1561, when Reval and the northern Estonian nobility submitted to Eric XIV during the collapse of the Livonian Confederation, until 1721. The Baltic German nobles kept their privileges and their Lutheran…

sweyn-forkbeard.s: Sweyn Forkbeard (c. 960–1014) was King of Denmark from about 986, after rebelling against his father Harald Bluetooth, and from 1000 also overlord of Norway.

syarif-abdurrahman-alkadrie.s: Syarif Abdurrahman Alkadrie (c. 1742–1808) was a trader of Hadrami Arab descent, son of a religious teacher, who founded Pontianak in western Borneo in 1771.

syarif-kasim-ii.s: Syarif Kasim II (1893–1968) was the twelfth and last Sultan of Siak Sri Indrapura in Sumatra, reigning from 1915. After Indonesian independence was proclaimed in 1945 he declared his support for the republic and handed over his state and much of his wealth.

sydir-bilyi.s: Sydir Bilyi (1735–1788) was a Zaporozhian Cossack officer who, after the destruction of the Zaporozhian Sich in 1775, became the first ataman of the Host of Loyal Zaporozhians formed by Grigory Potemkin in 1787. He led the Cossacks in the Russo-Turkish War and was mortally…

sylvanus-olympio.s: Sylvanus Olympio (1902–1963) was a Togolese businessman and nationalist who led French Togoland to independence. He headed the Committee of Togolese Unity, became prime minister after UN-supervised elections in 1958 and president of independent Togo in 1960.

symon-petliura.s: Symon Petliura (1879–1926) was a Ukrainian journalist and socialist politician who became the leading figure of the Ukrainian People's Republic. As commander of its army and from 1919 head of the Directorate, he fought the Bolsheviks and the Whites and in 1920 allied with Poland.
